subject: EMEA routing: EU data residency signals + playbook wording (pilot)
related_links: HubSpot workflow draft: PLG Signal -> Ownership (EMEA residency)
body:
From: Lukas Meyer <lukas_meyer@redwoodinference.com>
To: Isabelle Laurent <isabelle_laurent@redwoodinference.com>, Tyler Benson <tyler_benson@redwoodinference.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwoodinference.com>, Camila Reyes <camila_reyes@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Dr. Aisha Rahman <aisha.rahman@redwoodinference.com>, Markus Klein <markus@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Sun, May 18, 2025 at 09:12 AM +0100
Subject: EMEA routing: EU data residency signals + playbook wording (pilot)

Team — for the NA pilot we’re already routing by region, but we need to lock down how we handle EU data residency intent signals so we don’t (a) mis-route to NA, or (b) over-promise in wording.

Proposal (routing + packaging):

1) When to treat as “EU residency signal” (intent)
- Docs view(s) on EU residency / data processing location pages
- Security FAQ section: “data residency / EU region” clicks
- Any “VPC/Private” doc views from EU IP + explicit residency term in onsite search

2) Ownership rule
- Preserve existing HubSpot owner (AE/CSM) if already set
- Else if signal_type = EU_RESIDENCY_INTENT OR includes “residency=EU” tag, assign to EMEA queue (round robin)
- Regardless of owner, set property: plg_residency_requirement = “EU” so AE sees it on the company card

3) Required “attachments”/links for first-touch
- Data residency statement (public)
- Subprocessors list (public)
- DPA template (public)
- SOC 2 report: NOT attached; only share via NDA process

4) Playbook wording (draft) — needs review
Current draft line in playbook says: “We can guarantee all customer data stays in the EU.”
I think we need to soften to: “We can support EU data residency requirements via EU-hosted regions and Dedicated/Private deployments; we’ll confirm specifics based on your workload and deployment mode.”

Can Isabelle confirm ownership mapping for EMEA (esp. for accounts with NA HQ but EU residency needs)? Aisha, please confirm the approved set of docs we can proactively send.

Attaching current approved public artifacts (latest versions I have):
- Attachment: Redwood_EU_Data_Residency_Statement_v2.pdf
- Attachment: Redwood_Subprocessors_List_2025-05.pdf
- Attachment: Redwood_DPA_Template_2025-04.docx

Thanks,
Lukas Meyer
EMEA Sales
Redwood Inference


---

From: Isabelle Laurent <isabelle_laurent@redwoodinference.com>
To: Lukas Meyer <lukas_meyer@redwoodinference.com>, Tyler Benson <tyler_benson@redwoodinference.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwoodinference.com>, Camila Reyes <camila_reyes@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Dr. Aisha Rahman <aisha.rahman@redwoodinference.com>, Markus Klein <markus@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Sun, May 18, 2025 at 11:01 AM +0100
Subject: Re: EMEA routing: EU data residency signals + playbook wording (pilot)

Agree with direction.

Ownership mapping suggestions (to keep it deterministic and avoid ping-pong):

A) Preserve existing owner
- If company has HubSpot “Company owner” set (AE/CSM), do not overwrite.
- Add a task to that owner with the signal context and the “plg_residency_requirement=EU” property.

B) If no owner, assign by default rules
- If company country is in EEA/UK/CH OR signal explicitly EU_RESIDENCY_INTENT -> route to EMEA round-robin list.
- If company is US/Canada but EU residency signal (common: US HQ selling into EU):
  - Route stays with existing region logic IF an owner exists.
  - If no owner exists, still route to EMEA (because first convo tends to be residency + compliance).
  - Add note for handoff potential if commercial opportunity is NA-led (we can decide after discovery).

C) Re-notification/suppression
- Suppress repeat EU_RESIDENCY_INTENT tasks for 14 days unless signal_score increases materially (e.g., +20 points from pricing + security bundle).

One tweak: I’d prefer we don’t make the trigger “EU IP” alone. It’s too noisy (VPNs; consultants). EU IP should be an enhancer, not the primary trigger.

If you’re good with the above, I’ll update the routing rules section in the HubSpot spec.

— Isabelle
Sales Ops

From: Tyler Benson <tyler_benson@redwoodinference.com>
To: Lukas Meyer <lukas_meyer@redwoodinference.com>, Isabelle Laurent <isabelle_laurent@redwoodinference.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwoodinference.com>, Camila Reyes <camila_reyes@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Dr. Aisha Rahman <aisha.rahman@redwoodinference.com>, Markus Klein <markus@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Sun, May 18, 2025 at 12:26 PM +0100
Subject: Re: EMEA routing: EU data residency signals + playbook wording (pilot)

+1 on not using EU IP as the primary trigger.

On the “attachments” point: from deliverability + governance, we should avoid attaching compliance docs directly in outbound sequences when possible. Recommendation:
- Include links to the public docs (hosted on redwoodinference.com/security or our trust portal)
- Keep DPA as “available on request” or link to a gated form (so we have an audit trail)
- SOC 2 always via NDA gate + trust portal

If Aisha approves, I’ll add this as a “Marketing/Sales touch suppression + compliance assets distribution” note in the playbook so we keep the motion consistent across EMEA.

Tyler Benson
Marketing Ops

From: Dr. Aisha Rahman <aisha.rahman@redwoodinference.com>
To: Lukas Meyer <lukas_meyer@redwoodinference.com>, Isabelle Laurent <isabelle_laurent@redwoodinference.com>, Tyler Benson <tyler_benson@redwoodinference.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwoodinference.com>, Camila Reyes <camila_reyes@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Markus Klein <markus@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, May 19, 2025 at 08:17 AM +0100
Subject: Re: EMEA routing: EU data residency signals + playbook wording (pilot)

Confirming what’s OK to send without NDA:

Approved (public / pre-NDA):
- EU Data Residency Statement (OK)
- Subprocessors list (OK)
- High-level security overview page link (OK)

Not approved to attach/send pre-NDA:
- SOC 2 Type II report (must be via NDA + controlled sharing)
- Pen test reports (same)

Re: playbook wording — we should remove “guarantee” language unless we are in a contract/SOW context with the correct deployment mode.

Suggested safe wording:
- “We support EU data residency requirements through our EU regions and Dedicated/Private deployment options. We’ll confirm the specific data processing locations and logging/retention configuration based on your selected deployment mode and contract.”

Also, avoid saying “all data stays in EU” without clarifying what “data” means (prompt/response payloads vs metadata/logs) and what’s configurable.

Finally: please ensure the HubSpot note/task does not include sensitive customer data (no prompt content, no raw IP, no user emails). Only: signal type, date window, and non-PII account context.

Aisha
Security & Privacy

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwoodinference.com>
To: Lukas Meyer <lukas_meyer@redwoodinference.com>, Isabelle Laurent <isabelle_laurent@redwoodinference.com>, Tyler Benson <tyler_benson@redwoodinference.com>, Camila Reyes <camila_reyes@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Dr. Aisha Rahman <aisha.rahman@redwoodinference.com>, Markus Klein <markus@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, May 19, 2025 at 10:03 AM +0100
Subject: Re: EMEA routing: EU data residency signals + playbook wording (pilot)

Adding two playbook tweaks from the PLG side:

1) Make “EU residency intent” a tiered signal
- Medium intent: residency docs view only
- High intent: residency docs view + (pricing page OR Dedicated/Private docs OR repeated auth/security actions like API key rotation events)

2) Suggested discovery questions snippet (for AEs)
- “Is the requirement EU processing only, or also EU-only storage of logs/telemetry?”
- “Is this for a specific region (e.g., Germany) or broadly EEA?”
- “Are you looking for Hosted EU region, Dedicated EU capacity, or a private/VPC deployment?”

We can incorporate this into the playbook section so the first touch isn’t just sending docs.

Ben
Growth

From: Lukas Meyer <lukas_meyer@redwoodinference.com>
To: Isabelle Laurent <isabelle_laurent@redwoodinference.com>, Tyler Benson <tyler_benson@redwoodinference.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwoodinference.com>, Camila Reyes <camila_reyes@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Dr. Aisha Rahman <aisha.rahman@redwoodinference.com>, Markus Klein <markus@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, May 19, 2025 at 05:41 PM +0100
Subject: Re: EMEA routing: EU data residency signals + playbook wording (pilot)

This is super helpful — thank you.

Updated proposal (incorporating feedback):

Routing / ownership (for the router + HubSpot workflow):
- If Company owner exists -> preserve; create task + add “plg_residency_requirement=EU”
- Else if (company_country in EEA/UK/CH) OR (signal_type=EU_RESIDENCY_INTENT) -> assign EMEA round-robin
- EU IP address is NOT a trigger; only increases confidence when combined with the explicit docs/search signal
- Suppression: 14 days unless signal_score increases by >=20

Playbook wording replacement (remove guarantee):
- Replace with Aisha’s suggested safe wording (below) + add Ben’s discovery snippet.

Compliance assets distribution:
- First touch includes links to EU residency statement + subprocessors
- DPA: “available on request” (or a gated form) per Tyler’s note
- SOC2 always via NDA/trust portal

Aisha’s exact line (proposed):
“We support EU data residency requirements through our EU regions and Dedicated/Private deployment options. We’ll confirm the specific data processing locations and logging/retention configuration based on your selected deployment mode and contract.”

Isabelle — once you update the HubSpot spec, can you tag me for a final sanity check before we ask David to implement in workflows?

Lukas

From: Isabelle Laurent <isabelle_laurent@redwoodinference.com>
To: Lukas Meyer <lukas_meyer@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Tyler Benson <tyler_benson@redwoodinference.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwoodinference.com>, Camila Reyes <camila_reyes@redwoodinference.com>, Dr. Aisha Rahman <aisha.rahman@redwoodinference.com>, Markus Klein <markus@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, May 20, 2025 at 04:37 PM +0100
Subject: Re: EMEA routing: EU data residency signals + playbook wording (pilot)

Done — I’ve updated the HubSpot routing spec with:
- EU_RESIDENCY_INTENT routing logic (as you summarized)
- 14-day suppression + score delta override
- Note re: EU IP as confidence-only
- “No sensitive data in task notes” reminder

Next step: David can implement workflow changes when ready.

Also added the playbook wording replacement (no “guarantee”) and the assets distribution rules (links/gated request + NDA for SOC2).

— Isabelle
